text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden 5xx spike on /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1 (p95 latency also increased). Threshold breached: 12:10 UTC. Paging on-call: @alice.

alice: on it. looking at dashboards now, 5xx ~28% over last 2 mins. traces show a lot of KMS decrypt failures in the tokenization service.

ben: i just kicked a canary 09:58 UTC that updated the KMS alias env from `alias/redwood-prod` -> `alias/redwood-prod-v2` as part of key-rotation prep. deploys were small canary (5%) to tokenization svc.

carol: logs? paste a sample error.

ben: here's the stack tail:```
error=KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException, User: arn:aws:sts::1111111111:assumed-role/redwood-deploy is not authorized to use key alias/redwood-prod-v2
name=tokenization svc
pod=token-5f9f4b
```

alice: ok looks like the new alias isn't usable by the runtime role. either key-policy missing the role or the alias points to a key with restrictive policy. can we flip the canary off (kill-switch) to stop new pods from using v2?

ben: feature flag `tokenizer.kms_alias` was gated via rollout. i'm toggling the canary flag to `off` now.

deploy-bot: Received toggle request for feature `tokenizer.kms_alias` -> off. Starting staged rollout (10s intervals).

support-bot: initial customer impact: ~1.2% of incoming requests failed with 500 (errors correlated with tokenization). A handful of customers reported degraded UX: search and chat responses failing. ticket count rising.

carol: good mitigation plan but we should also prepare rollback in case flag toggle doesn't drain errors fast enough. ben can you trigger a rollback of canary revision to 0?

ben: starting rollback to revision `r2026-09-14_7` for tokenization svc.```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/tokenization --to-revision=20260914-7
```

ben: rollback initiated. monitoring pods restart.

alice: monitoring errors -- after flag toggle the 5xx dropped to 5% in 30s, after rollback dropped to ~0.5% now. p95 latency returning to baseline.

dave: for long-term, we need a pre-deploy check that validates key policies for any alias referenced in env/secret changes. i saw the helm values used the new alias but the KMS key wasn't granted the `redwood-runtime` principal.

carol: agree. action items: (1) preflight check script for KMS alias + key policy (2) require key-policy validation in deploy CI (3) improve runbook to prefer flag kill-switch + rollback order.

support-bot: updated customer impact: ~4200 requests affected across 3 hours window, ~0.03% of total traffic. top affected tenants: acme-inc, widgetco. CS is sending status updates.

alice: handing off to carol for the next on-call shift and postmortem. key details captured in incident doc draft: include deploy revision, alias name `alias/redwood-prod-v2`, IAM principal missing.

carol: ack. i'll own postmortem and coordinate follow-ups with security to update key policy and with deploy infra to add CI checks.

incident-bot: Incident resolved and marked SEVERITY=low. Root cause: new KMS alias used by canary lacked runtime IAM permission. Mitigation: feature flag kill-switch + deployment rollback. Postmortem owner: carol.

alice: leaving note: if you need to repro quickly, see test script `tools/kms-preflight-check.sh` local stub i used to validate policy (will push to repo).

ben: will coordinate a safe re-roll after policies are patched; tagging infra-security and deploy-team. :white_check_mark:

carol: handing off final tasks in the ticket tracker. closing channel for active ops but will keep thread for PM/pm follow-up.
